name: AS/NZS 3112 (Type I)
description: Australian and New Zealand household plug and socket system: two flat blades set at 30° to the vertical in an inverted V, and a vertical flat earth pin below. Rated 10 A in its basic form, with 15, 20, 25 and 32 A variants whose wider or reshaped pins keep a higher-rated plug out of a lower-rated socket.

variants.name: AS/NZS 3112 10 A plug
variants.keying: The inverted-V blades and the earth pin allow one orientation only.
mechanicalNotes: Active and neutral blades about 6.35 × 1.6 mm, at 30° to the vertical, centred 7.92 mm from the plug centre.
Earth pin centred 10.31 mm below the plug centre, slightly longer than the blades.
Active and neutral blades carry insulating sleeves since the 2000 revision of the standard.
Blade lengths differ between secondary sources (17.06 mm or 17.35 mm); not recorded.

variants.name: AS/NZS 3112 10 A socket-outlet
variants.keying: Inverted-V slots and earth slot accept the plug one way only; the earth slot rejects the wider earth pin of 15 A and higher plugs.
mechanicalNotes: Flush socket-outlet; mounting orientation is earth slot down.

notes: Ratings and dimensions rely on secondary sources citing AS/NZS 3112:2017; neither the 2017 nor the current 2025 edition was reviewed.
Rated voltage is not stated by the cited sources (they give the nominal supply only), so it is null.
Frequency is not stated for the configuration (the sources give 50 Hz as the supply frequency of the countries).

Active/neutral sides conflict between two secondary sources: one puts the active on the left looking into the socket with the earth down, the other says the top-right pin is active. The drawing therefore labels both blade slots L/N.
The 20 A, 25 A and 32 A variants (wider pins, L- or U-shaped earth pin) are not modelled yet.
Argentina (IRAM 2073) and China (GB 1002) use a near-identical layout with different pin lengths and, in Argentina, reversed polarity; they are not part of this family.
